articles.content:
Adil El Arbi and Bilall Fallah , the Belgian directing duo behind 2020's smash hit sequel “Bad Boys for Life” starring Will Smith and Martin Lawrence, have invested in award-winning production company “ Caviar .”

The two have taken a minority stake in the fellow Belgian outfit, joining as shareholders through their banner Los Morros.

Over the last 20 years Caviar, also based in Belgium, has worked in both the scripted, non-scripted and branded space, and is best known for “Sound of Metal,” which was nominated for six Oscars in 2020, including best film, winning best sound and best film editing. Other projects include Zach Woods' upcoming “The Accompanist,” which premiered at Tribeca, and “The Best Immigrant,” exec produced by both Arbi and Fallah. Arbi and Fallah have a long history with Caviar, which produced their breakthrough feature “Black.” Since then, the pair directing “Bad Boys for Life” ($426M worldwide) and its sequel “Bad Boys Ride or Die” ($405M), plus "Ms. Marvel" for Disney+, "Snowfall" for FX and “Rebel,” which premiered in Cannes. They also directed “Batgirl,” which was controversially shelved while in post-production at Warner Bros. as part of David Zaslav's cost-cutting.

Added Caviar CEO Bert Hamelinck: "Caviar is and remains a talent-driven production company. Welcoming Adil and Bilall strengthens our creative core and supports our growth strategy. We're delighted to take this step together."

articles.title: Florence Pugh Fires Back at Video Claiming She Used Plastic Surgery to Change Her Face: 'Disturbing' How 'People Can't Tell the Difference Between Aging and Surgery'

The Oscar nominee left a comment on an Instagram video posted by Evie magazine in which she called it "disturbing" how people can no longer tell the difference between natural aging and plastic surgery. articles.content:
Florence Pugh is shutting down speculation over whether or not she's had plastic surgery done to her face. The Oscar nominee left a comment on an Instagram video posted by Evie magazine in which she called it “disturbing” how people can no longer tell the difference between natural aging and plastic surgery. The video called into question whether or not Pugh changed her face shape by going under the knife.

“Guys. I turned 30. I'm a woman. Body's and faces change. It's not that deep,” Pugh wrote. “The fact that people can't even tell between what's aging and what's surgery is disturbing. Sadly puppy fluff doesn't last forever.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Macaulay Culkin Returns as Kevin McCallister in McDonalds' 'Home Alone' Christmas Ad

In the video posted by Evie magazine , a female commenter is superimposed in front of two pictures of Pugh that are used to show how plastic surgery might've changed the actor's face shape.

“Is this a safe space? People are saying Florence Pugh has fallen victim to Hollywood's war on round faces,” the Evie commentator says. “Don't get me wrong, Florence Pugh still looks beautiful, but I think we can all collectively agree that Hollywood seems to have this thing against softer features. The desirable thing in the entertainment industry and the modeling industry right now is this sculpted, snatched looked. A lot of people are pointing out how Florence used to have full, beautiful cheeks that made her face super recognizable. Now that her jaw is more defined, her chin is pointier and her jaw is more sharp, it makes sense why people are wondering if she had work done.”

The commentator added later in the video, “What hurts me the most about this is young women seeing [Pugh's face] and thinking, ‘Oh, my naturally soft features are something that need to be fixed and its undesirable.'” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Pugh is not one to stand down against social media speculation and/or bullying over her appearance. In Aug. 2023, for instance, she notably railed against the backlash she was getting for exposing skin either in movies or on the red carpet. One year prior, Pugh wore a see-through dress at a Valentino couture show in Rome and had to use Instagram to condemn "vulgar" trolls who sought out to "totally destroy a woman's body."

“I think the scariest thing for me are the instances where people have been upset that I've shown ‘too much' of myself,” she said in 2013. “When everything went down with the Valentino pink dress a year ago, my nipples were on display through a piece of fabric, and it wound people up. It's the freedom that people are scared of; the fact I'm comfortable and happy."

Pugh continued, "Keeping women down by commenting on their bodies has worked for a very long time. I think we're in this swing now where lots of people are saying, ‘I don't give a shit.' Unfortunately, we've become so terrified of the human body that we can't even look at my two little cute nipples behind fabric in a way that isn't sexual. We need to keep reminding everybody that there is more than one reason for women's bodies [to exist]."

In a Dec. 2024 interview with The Sunday Times , Pugh called it "exhausting" to be a young woman in Hollywood and added at the time: "I remember godawful headlines about how Keira Knightley isn't thin anymore, or watching women getting torn apart despite being talented and beautiful. The only thing people want to talk about is some useless crap about how they look. And so I didn't care to abide by those rules."

Pugh is gearing up for a busy rest of the year with the same-day releases of “ Avengers: Doomsday ” and “ Dune: Part Three ,” both of which hit theaters on Dec. 18.

The world is currently being swept up by the latest Grand Theft Auto video game, but could the record-setting franchise one day be a TV series or movie? The answer, according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick: Maybe, in the right circumstances.

Prior to Grand Theft Auto 6 breaking pre-sales records ahead of its official global release tomorrow, Zelnick was asked about “line extensions” for the gaming franchise during a recent appearance on The David Rubenstein Show podcast – to which he gave a measured response.

“We're very careful about line extensions because this is a creative company and our goal is to make the best entertainment on earth – entertainment we're always proud of,” said Zelnick. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Video Games 'Grand Theft Auto VI' Turns Chaos & Crime Into Cash & Clout With Record-Shattering Launch News Microsoft "Deeply Sorry" About Global Outlook Outage, Insists Disruption Caused By "Network Capacity Upgrade"

Top-selling video games have become solid bases for TV and film adaptations, with Netflix taking The Witcher to multiple seasons, HBO gaining critical acclaim for its version of The Last of Us and the likes of Super Mario Bros , Sonic the Hedgehog and Minecraft all having successful movies released in recent years. Elden Rings was recently being shopped at the American Film Market.

articles.content:
India's "How Love Moves" won the Al Jazeera Documentary Co-Production Award Wednesday at the prizegiving ceremony of Forum, the co-production and co-financing market of leading documentary festival IDFA .

Pallavi Paul's film centers on a century-old graveyard in New Delhi, where the "slow seeping poison of communal hatred and the everyday beauty and brutality of the city come to a head, while an unassuming gravekeeper wages a lone struggle to preserve the sanctity of the dead." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Macaulay Culkin Returns as Kevin McCallister in McDonalds' 'Home Alone' Christmas Ad

It is produced by Aman Mann and Shaunak Sen for Kiterabbit Films.

The award, which recognizes "projects addressing an urgent issue of our time" presented in the Pitch or Roundtable categories, comes with a $25,000 prize.

Jury members Mohamed Elmongy and Brigid O'Shea said the project, which they described as "politically and creatively sophisticated," explored "the vulnerability of communities deemed dangerous and wrong through state-inflicted violence."

They added, "In doing so, we believe audiences around the world will have access to a place and the people living there who otherwise we may never encounter, and correct or add a new layer of complexity beyond the mainstream narrative.

"And more importantly, it is an exciting opportunity to support a woman-director's voice, we hope at a critical junction in the life of her project."

Alina Baitokova's "Stitch by Stitch" from Kyrgyzstan received the ARTE European Talent Development Award, which comes with a €10,000 prize. The award recognizes a project in development or early production presented in the Pitch or Roundtable categories of IDFA Forum. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The film follows Elmira, a single mother and seamstress in an informal sewing workshop in Kyrgyzstan, who struggles to make ends meet while trying to rebuild the fragile bonds with her children after years of painful separation.

The producer is Adilet Karzhoev for Karzhoev Films, and the co-producers are Marianna Kaat for Baltic Film Production and Christian Popp for Tanjo Films.

Jury members Olga Chernykh, Anne-Laure Négrin and Hanne Phlypo said, "We decided to award a project from a country whose stories are rarely told, with high need of support right now, and to give a director tools to move the project ahead and tell the story that shows people struggling for their life in a rarely seen part of the globalization. It's a film brought by a promising team, a delicate emerging voice."

Parsa Ansari's "Shooting Stars" from Iran received the IDFA Forum Award for best pitch project, which is accompanied by a €1,500 prize.

In the film, a boy begins to question who the real aliens are while investigating mysterious UFO sightings from his childhood. His search gradually shifts from extraterrestrial fantasies toward the invisible outsiders living among us on Earth.

It is produced by Milad Khosravibaledi for Seven Springs Pictures, in co-production with Thibaut Amri for Avant la Nuit, Steven Rubinstein Malamud for Grom Productions, Maria Robstad Nielsen for Emjay Productions and Anita Norfolk for Folk Film.

Jury members Nicolas van Hemelryck and Zane Krūmiņa said, it is "a personal and emotional story where imagination and artistic originality intersect. It is an inspiring narrative about the artist's creative journey that can serve as an encouragement for the young generation."

The IDFA Forum Award for Best Roundtable Project was awarded to Daniela Muñoz Barroso's "Silence Diaries" from Spain and Cuba. The award is accompanied by a €1,500 prize.

The autobiographical documentary traces "a journey in search of a new language" and explores the director's "experience of uprootedness and the gradual loss of sound until the birth of my daughter."

The producers are Muñoz Barroso and Leila Montero for Estudio ST, in co-production with Efthymia Zymvragaki for Gris Medio.

Jury members Renko Douze and Mariia Ponomarova said, "Taking full command of its medium, this project struck us with its artistic strength, evocative approach and sharp conceptual thinking, all within a highly intimate film. Through gesture, rhythm and mesmerizing imagery, the filmmaker convincingly weaves three separate threads, and in doing so tells a deeply personal story with remarkable agency and sensitivity." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Nikos Pilos and Arsinoi Pilou's "Resisting Residents" from Greece received the award for Best Rough Cut Project, which is accompanied by a €1,500 prize.

The logline reads: "In the heart of Athens, a community resists, survives and redefines solidarity."

The producer is Dafni Kalafati for Filmiki.

Jury members Chalida Uabumrungjit and Cleo Veger said, " ‘Resisting Residents' is a powerful reminder of how cinema can champion what we believe in. This brave documentary captures a community standing firm for their homes, their dignity and their right to live together, proving that film can be an essential voice for justice and human solidarity.

"We were moved by the courage of the residents, who take in newcomers, face their own conflicts and fight eviction together, and by a film team honest enough to show all of it. Shot by a two-person crew living inside the community, it's close, trusting and alive, and we can't wait to see it finished."

The IDFA DocLab Forum Award for Best Project went to "This Pleasant Lady" by Victoria Mapplebeck. The award is accompanied by a €1,500 prize.

The U.K. project is a coming-of-age story, said the director, "in which, at 61, I write my ‘fuck you' list, learn to love again and stop being pleasant. An immersive journey through my brain, breasts and heart becomes a defiant celebration of survival, desire and late-middle-aged rebellion."

It is produced by Mapplebeck for First Person Films.

Jury members Min-Wei Kuo and David Massey said, "The jury unanimously agrees that this project is inspirational and addresses serious subjects in an irreverent but impactful way that will engage with audiences no matter of their cultural background or ages. The spirit of the project and the artist fits the vibe of IDFA DocLab. We're also now encouraged to create our own fuck you list!"

Grand Theft Auto is finally back.

The sixth edition in the long-running Rockstar Games series returned this morning, and it has earned rave reviews from critics.

In a glowing New York Times review titled Grand Theft Auto VI Will Steal Your Heart, writer Yussef Cole said the game showed "surprising depth," anchored by its two main characters, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, and a rich in-game world.

"Written, programmed and performed by a cast and crew of tens of thousands, Grand Theft Auto VI is more than a typical video game; it is a great gathering of art forms and talent, an unruly, comprehensive cultural atlas of American life and manners," the newspaper said. "Its triumph lies in encounters I just described, where race, class, gender, money and attention shape our circumstances and what we decide to do about them."

articles.summary: With the news that Tom Hiddleston would be appearing in Avengers: Doomsday, Loki fans were understandably concerned that the movie would ruin the show (or the entire character), but Hiddleston's recent update should bring those fans some comfort. Already, audiences have gotten a sneak peek at what Loki's Doomsday role might entail. Specifically, Loki was […]
articles.content:
This suggests that Loki will be operating as his God of Stories self, presumably arriving because Steve has decided to stay in the past and has therefore created issues within the multiverse. After all, it's already been confirmed that Steve's decision to stay in the past caused Doomsday . Even with this context from Endgame Encore , though, fans had serious concerns about what Loki's role in the movie would mean for the perfect conclusion to his story in Loki , which saw him finally find his “glorious purpose.” Thankfully, Hiddleston has himself just confirmed that he won't be letting that story be undermined in Doomsday . Check out his exact comments below.

After so many years of Loki dying (or fake dying) and coming back, moving between a villain and something like a hero, and suffering various losses, it was honestly very satisfying to see him find his way in Loki , especially because it didn't feel forced; it felt like a natural progression for the character. It's therefore understandable that fans are worried about what Doomsday will mean for that satisfying conclusion. However, speaking with Empire Magazine , Hiddleston reportedly shared, “I feel very protective of the character. I don't want to unstitch anything.” It doesn't come as a huge surprise that Hiddleston will be protective of the character, as he has long been vocal about caring deeply about Loki.

It's the second part of these comments in particular that is important, though. The idea that Hiddleston isn't letting anything be “unstitched” specifically implies that the end of Loki will be protected. In light of that, it seems like Doomsday will simply be building upon what Loki has already set up in terms of Loki's role in the multiverse. In fact, while it's not clear at this point whether Loki is a projection or really physically present, it would make sense that Loki needed to intervene in Steve's decision and would keep his position as the God of Stories very much intact, as long as it's done right. Of course, there are other questions, such as whether Thor and Loki will come back together, as many MCU fans are hoping will be the case. Thankfully, these mysteries will only remain for a short while longer, as Doomsday hits theaters in exactly one month.

What do you hope to see in terms of Loki's story in Doomsday ? Let us know in the comments down below.

articles.title: A Mischief of Magpies #3 Is a Moving, Perfect Finale to an All Time Fantasy Great [REVIEW]
articles.summary: Earlier this year, one of the best fantasy comics in recent memory, A Mischief of Magpies, made its debut. From Simon Spurrier and Matias Bergara and published by DSTLRY, the first issue introduced readers to Mar, a teen boy dealing with a stunning secret in that every so often and entirely without warning, he falls […]
articles.content:
A Mischief of Magpies #3 opens in a dark place, though not a surprising one. While most of the series is spent in the fantastical city, we have been getting bits and pieces of Mar’s real life throughout as well and what is implied at the end of issue #2 is made very clear at the start of #3 with the teen having made an attempt on his own life. However, this is not just a story of a troubled teen and a grim attempt to end one’s own life. What is brilliant about A Mischief of Magpies #3 — and the series as a whole — is that this is much more a story about understanding of self and healing on one’s own terms and while tragedy is our starting point, this issue and this finale is one of what might be the most beautiful human story of all: triumph.

I’m not going to dig fully into the details of Mar’s return to the city or how he comes to figure out what it fully represents. One of the beautiful things about A Mischief of Magpies as a story, but this issue in particular, is that the revelations need to play out in real time with the reader. But something that works very well with this story is that even if you know what is coming (ComicBook was able to read the entire series back in March ahead of release), it still feels like a surprise and a fresh twist. The credit to that goes to the details. Both in terms of Spurrier’s words and Bergara’s art, A Mischief of Magpies is a book of details where every single one has meaning, those meanings matter, and they all contribute to the mystery and the reveal. In Issue #3, we finally find out what the mysterious MAP markings have meant and it’s that revelation that not only unlocks a way forward for Mar, but it makes full sense of everything we’ve seen before.

The best thing about A Mischief of Magpies #3, however, might be how Mar’s fantasy world and reality are pulled together at last. It’s no secret at this point in the story that the book is a tale about mental health but this also isn’t a story where the resolution of Mar’s depression is a simple victory over darkness. In the real world, we see the heavy toll Mar’s suffering has taken on him while in the fantasy world we see the struggle and the weight of it from the inside. Spurrier does a phenomenal and haunting job of putting into words what it is like to hit the absolute rock bottom of all rock bottoms and still look up and, art-wise, there is a moment where Mar comes to fully understand himself and his eternal challenges and quite literally embraces his darkness that Bergara’s art makes so beautiful it hurts — and it’s all done in the gorgeous context of a layered, well-crafted fantasy.

A Mischief of Magpies #3 is a rare case where a final issue not only sticks the landing but fully completes its story. It remains as immersive as it was from the very first page of the very first issue and it keeps its sense of magic even as the story’s darkness is fully laid bare. This is a stunning, haunting, gorgeous, and essential book in a series that deserves to be considered an all-time great. I genuinely do not know how Spurrier and Bergara will ever top this tale.

A Mischief of Magpies #3 is on sale now from DSTLRY.

articles.content:
Taylor Swift and AI investment have proven to be a big boosts to the U.S. economy in the recent years. Yet, come Thursday, the mayhem packed Grand Theft Auto VI is going to be the heavy hitter with record breaking stats and a possibly legislative long-tail that could truly change the game.

Or, as they've been saying repeatedly this midterms mocking season on Comedy Central's South America (a.k.a. South Park ): "If you ask me, this whole country has gone to sh*t …But hopefully things will get better in November. That's when Grand Theft Auto VI comes out."

Exceeding $1.54 billion in pre-order sales, according to market intelligence firm Sensor Tracker, the first new game in the GTA video game franchise in 13 years is already the most successful entertainment industry launch ever. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); } Related Stories News Netflix UK Swoops For Ms Apple's Pre-School Learning Adventures News Jeff Bezos Describes How Amazon Decided On Robert Pattinson As The Next James Bond

Put in franchise perspective, GTA VI' s pre-order haul is just a touch under double the launch of the $800 million snared by 2013's Grand Theft Auto V , the previous all-time entertainment debut record holder. GTA V, which like GTA VI was pushed back from its originally stated release date, has gone on to sell more than 235 million units. The sometimes grisly GTA V has also proved a massive hit on publisher Rockstar Games ‘ lucrative GTA Online multiplayer platform.

To give you an idea of the massive numbers in store here for GTA VI ‘s first day when it comes to the big screen, the global box office opening day alone this year on Sony/Marvel Studio's Spider-Man: Brand New Day was $276.1 million (note that some foreign territories open on Wednesday and Thursday and have their ticket sales rolled into North America's opening day Friday). Spider-Man: Brand New Day went on to post a global opening weekend of $932 million and that's the second highest worldwide opening at the B.O. After Avengers: Endgame's $1.2 billion. Five movies have grossed over $1 billion worldwide year-to-date, Brand New Day being the highest at $2.5 billion, ahead of The Odyssey ($1.8 billion), Toy Story ($1.1 billion), biopic Michael ($1 billion) and Super Mario Galaxy Movie ($1 billion). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

At the current trajectory leading to GTA VI going live at midnight local time globally on November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, pre-orders are on target to hit sales of 20 million and $2 billion in revenue before the end of the week. Before the end of the year, with day of launch purchases and then holiday shopping factoring in, GTA IV is estimated to bring in around $3 billion, says L.A.-based Wedbush Securities.

“Next to James Bond , there might not be another franchise of this scale that has been as consistent with its brand,” says Larry Vincent, professor of Marketing at USC Marshall School of Business. “It's like they apprenticed with the Broccali family,” he adds of the Take-Two Interactive owned series and the former 007 bosses.

Kinder and gentler in execution than past sex worker killing and explicit content containing installments of the 1997 originating open sandbox franchise, the still very violent GTA VI finds the detail rich immersive series returning to the Miami-inspired Vice City. Which means, much like 2002's single player Grand Theft Auto: Vice City , the ever-expanding crime escapades of lovers Jason and Lucia in this iteration are neon streaked, car chase fueled, bullet loaded and blood soaked in the sweaty fictional state of Leonida.

Filled to the brim with a satirical and scathing take on American culture. GTA VI is clearly giving the people the blood and circus' they want.

Following a leak online, the December 4, 2025 release of the official GTA VI trailer racked up over 93 million views in 24 hours to become the all-time top non-music debut on the Alphabet-owned video platform. Philadelphia-based Comcast this week declared the first 48 hours of GTA VI pre-order downloads that began on November 10 to be “our network's biggest event and two of its 10 busiest days ever.”

Managing pre-order downloads and expecting a rush of launch day purchases, Stateside internet providers such as Charter ‘s Spectrum and Comcast's Xfinity have been offering customers free speed boasts to prevent digital logjams. Add to that, as Sony put out last minute PS5 software updates, a worry for later in the week is that the internet could slow due to spike in YouTube livestreams and social media posts as players drill into the game.

A true global release, GTA VI nearly crashed Netflix this summer with its well watched Extended Look featurette . As proof of the streamer's own clout and reach, GTA VI pre-sales surged once the 27-minute Extended Look dropped on August 27.

Since then, promotion for the game has covered almost every digital, horizontal and vertical surface from L.A. to NYC to London, Paris, Berlin, New Delhi, Hong Kong, Tokyo and Sydney and all points in between.

With skyscrapers, hoardings and murals all over the seven continents displaying GTA VI artwork, product activations soared. Songs from the game has topped playlists too, with a soundtrack score by electronic duo Justice out on December 11.

Going local, the game logo has skinned the outside of the arena of the NBA's Miami Heat. Inside the Kaseya Center, GTA VI will be all over Wednesday's “A Night in Vice City” ESPN broadcasted game between the Heat and the Milwaukee Bucks.

No details have been revealed yet as to when the more than $1 billion to develop GTA VI will appear on the GTA Online platform. The presumption is it will likely be deep into 2027 to give Take-Two's bottom line a multi-quarter leg up. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

Take-Two shares gained 6% last week amid the GTA hype, but have since reversed direction. They fell 4% on Tuesday and are now down 20% in 2026 to date as Wall Street has sought to reconcile the runaway success of the GTA franchise with decidedly mixed quarterly financial results. Take-Two aren't the only ones feeling the pinch. All video game publishers have been scrambling of late to adjust to an evolving consumer marketplace, with mobile and casual games meaningfully eating into the share of traditional console tentpoles.

With that, any deeper bottom line comparisons between MAGA era GTA VI and the Obama Era GTA V does become a little bit apples to avocados.

To frustration of some, the 2026 game is only available digitally as opposed to on the more traditional disc of previous GTA s. Which is also why, if you are a gamer or gamer adjacent, you have spent days over the past week downloading the colossal 212GB GTA VI for Thursday's debut. In anticipation of November 19, which is widely viewed as an adult snow day with millions of fans playing hooky off work to play the game, you may have also been forking out more cash to upgrading your console so you can play GTA VI in either its $79.99 Standard Edition or the $99.99 Ultimate Edition.

It is that money pit mentality from the video game industry that spurned Rep. Ritchie Torres (D-NY) to put the Power to the Players Act before Congress last month. Still collecting co-sponsors and paused a bit as a newly Democratic-controlled majority prepares to take power, the P2P Act would compel the FCC to ensure that buying a game means it's the consumer's, full stop.

“Just based on revenue, the video game industry is larger than global film, global music, and North American sports combined,” the just re-elected South Bronx representing Democrat says. “It's massive, and historically, it's been the most affordable form of entertainment,” the Congressman asserts. “My district is hit the hardest by the affordability crisis, and digital-only distribution disproportionately disadvantages the lowest-income consumers, who are more likely to trade and use games to subsidize the purchase of new ones.”

In a stance that runs counter to where Take-Two and much of the industry are taking things, Rep. Torrs adds: “My view is that in a properly functioning marketplace, when you pay for a video game, you should be purchasing the game itself, right? If you pay for it, then you should own it. Simple rule, but increasingly, when you pay for a video game, you are not purchasing the game itself. You are purchasing a license to play the game, and that license can be revoked arbitrarily at the discretion of the gaming company. So, it feels to me like we as consumers are paying higher and higher prices while enjoying fewer and fewer rights, if any rights at all.”

Torres' bill has a way to go before becoming a law, but it is certainly now part of the cultural conversation sparked by GTA VI ‘s mega-release As close to a monoculture moment as we can have in 2026, GTA VI is a conversation even the cops and the Weather Channel have joined:

Another voice in all this belongs to producer and actor Matthew Waterson. Best known as the voice of X-Men '97 ‘s Magneto, Waterson is also an alum of the blockbuster Call of Duty franchise and Rockstar's best selling Red Dead Redemption games. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

“They're such unique properties that people are willing to wait for, people are willing to talk about, think about it and get excited for because they build such rich environments,” Waterson insists of GTA and RDR . “Most other companies at this point don't have the the time or the money or the capital to do that,”

“These big public companies don't have the capital expenditure abilities to put 10 years into a huge world concept game if they don't know it's going to make money,” says Waterson of risk adverse and cash restricted studios and streamers. “Rockstar have two products that they know are going to make money. Rockstar can do that, and just about nobody else can.”

articles.title: X-Orcists #1 Kicks Off This Unique New Mutant Book With a Banger (Review)
articles.summary: The X-Men books have been in flux since the summer of 2024, when the Krakoa Era ended and the Brevoort era began. With the team heading to the MCU, Marvel put their most trusted executive editor, Tom Brevoort, in the X-Office. He's gained a reputation for launching successful series for the publisher, but his time […]
articles.content:
X-Orcists is Brevoort's latest attempt to diversify the mutant line, going back to a well that was honestly kind of unsuccessful – mutant magic. While magic-using mutants have been around for ages, it was the dawn of the Krakoa Era that saw it brought to the fore again and flounder completely. However, this time it looks like it might actually work, as Allen teams with artist German Peralta for a first issue that will knock your socks off.

It feels like I write about Ashley Allen a lot and honestly, I'm pretty happy about it. I have not been all-in on the Brevoort era X-Office – quite the opposite, really – but Allen's work has been impressing me every time I read a new book of hers. She gets these characters and is able to create compelling narratives for them. This issue is another example of that, as she drops us in a county fair gone wrong, and then keeps ramping things up from there, leading to Magik, Maddie, and Juggernaut battling a body-hopping demon. It's a fun, fast-paced action story, with Allen throwing in little glimpses of the plot as the heroes realize what's going on, leading to a surprising ending that brings back a villain I actually asked for not all that long ago.

This issue would have been a perfect comic for me, but then we get to Madelyne Pryor. Madelyne Pryor is integral to X-history in a number of ways and she's been played as a monster for years, an evil, sexual woman who tried to kill her child and cheated on her husband with his brother (anyone remember when she was seducing the alternate universe version of her son? People have real problems with Madelyne Pryor slander). However, Maddie is as much a victim as anyone else – she was manipulated and maneuvered, and, lest we forget, abandoned by her husband Cyclops, who is going through something of a renaissance with fans. They were starting to play her more as the victim she is in the Krakoa Era and I was happy with that, but in this book Allen goes back somewhat to the monster Maddie, the one who doesn't trust herself, and everyone sees as the ravening Goblin Queen. I think the change to Cyclops as the always right leader everyone loves is a part of that – admitting Maddie's a victim means admitting that her crimes are Cyclops's fault – and Brevoort seemingly isn't about to let anyone do that with the mutant leader. Your mileage may vary on this one, but it was enough for me to penalize the comic.

German Peralta and Allen worked together on Magik and have seemingly created a pretty good shorthand between the two of them. Peralta's one of those artists who has been soldiering away at the B-list Marvel books for a bit now. We've been able to watch his development as an artist and X-Orcists is a perfect example of how good he's gotten. Allen handed him a script full of big demonic action and he took it with a smile, giving readers an exciting comic that brings the story to life beautifully.

His line work is confident; this is an artist who knows where he wants everything to go and it shows in each panel. His lines are strong and smooth, his figure work is gorgeous, and his characters acting gets the point across. He even does his best to not overly sexualize Maddie, which is honestly pretty nice for a change. His action scenes have a nice fluid quality, which especially helps with an issue that has so much action in it. I love that he doesn't skimp out on the backgrounds, like some other artists do at times. He's able to capture the feel of small town fairgrounds so well you can smell frying oil and exhaust from the diesel generators, their low-pitched rumble playing in your ears, before the fire and screams take over.

X-Orcists is a book that could have went the direction of Excalibur/Knights of X/Captain Britain went – meaning blah stories that only people who shipped Betsy and Rachel liked – but instead is able to blend the ideas of mutant and magic much better than that trilogy of books. Magik, Madelyne Pryor, and Juggernaut are all characters who deserve more spotlight and Allen does a fantastic job with each of them (I might not like her Maddie direction, but she does capture the essence of the character). Peralta's art makes it all work, giving readers the kind of imagery that makes stories like this sing. Putting these three characters together for a trip into the darkness of Limbo, by these two creators, was an excellent idea and I can't wait to see where it goes next.

articles.title: DOC NYC Doc ‘Dryads,’ From Mallorca-Based Miguel Eeks, Explores ‘the Mystery of Creation Through Music’

articles.content:
Competing at prominent documentary fest DOC NYC, which also hosts its international premiere, Miguel Eek's "Dryads" ("Dríades") ponders the mystery of musical creation as he follows three indie musicians, Vasco Ribeiro from Portugal, Joana Gomila in Mallorca and Norway's Emil Karlsen, as they source their music from their environs and local traditions.

Produced by Mallorca-based Mosaic, "Dryads" focuses on the creative process behind their works: Karlsen, a young Sámi musician and multi-instrumentalist, seeks inspiration for his joiks, the time-honored songs of his culture, in the fjords and tundra of northern Norway; Gomila explores the acoustic mysteries of caves, abandoned buildings and the expressive possibilities of the human voice, while Ribeiro, also known as Omiri, reworks traditional Portuguese music into something more modern and uniquely his own. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Taiwan Creative Content Fest Takeaways: 'Avatar' VFX House Brings Its AI Ambitions to Taipei as Character IP Booms Hollywood Has Flipped on GenAI, Says 'Avatar' VFX House Weta FX Chief: 'If You Don’t Have an AI Strategy, Don’t Bother'

Despite their different approaches, all three share a common curiosity: how music comes into being, and how tradition, experimentation, improvisation and individual expression come together to create something new.

Through "Dryads," Eek continues his exploration of observational cinema and its capacity to capture human experience through intimacy and shared time.

His most recent film, "Amílca r " premiered at IDFA , where it received the Outstanding Artistic Contribution Award in the Envision Competition.

He delved further into the making of his film with Variety:

You describe the act of making music as something almost mysterious. Did spending time with these musicians change the way you understand your own creative process as a filmmaker? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

It was, in many ways, a journey of discovery. I wanted to explore the mystery of creation through music, which I have always considered perhaps the most mysterious of all art forms.

What I discovered, particularly through the time I spent with these musicians, was how many similarities there are between their creative processes and mine. Listening, for instance, is the first step towards creation. Joana, Emil and Vasco devote a great deal of time to inhabiting places, observing and listening to their surroundings, allowing landscapes and the people who inhabit them to offer clues about the music that will eventually emerge.

This made me realize that creation does not necessarily originate within ourselves. It also comes from what surrounds us, from our capacity to pay attention and to remain receptive to the world. I found many more parallels with my own experience of documentary filmmaking than I had anticipated.

All three musicians work outside the mainstream music industry, working with both inherited traditions and contemporary tools. Do you see their independence as an artistic choice, a necessity, or a way of resisting the increasingly standardized nature of the music business?

From the beginning, I wanted to explore forms of creation beyond the pressures of the music industry. I find it difficult to imagine these musicians preserving their freedom in terms of time, experimentation and working methods within increasingly standardized structures. Their independence is not simply an act of resistance; it allows a different approach to creation, rooted in craftsmanship, patience and a close relationship with their surroundings. For me, this is both a political and artistic choice: protecting the conditions in which something genuinely unexpected can emerge.

How do you balance observational intimacy and trust with the inevitable influence of the camera and filmmaking team on the creative process?

In ‘Dryads,' I return to a working method developed in previous films, beginning with a pact of trust with the people I film. I then maintain a relatively static, unobtrusive presence. Over time, life and the creative process take over, and our small crew becomes part of the landscape. We never disappear completely, but we stop being a source of disturbance. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I don't believe complete observational distance exists, nor should it be the goal. What matters is building a relationship in which the camera does not fundamentally alter the process being filmed. That is when a certain authenticity becomes possible, and the material that ultimately matters in the editing room begins to emerge.

The landscapes in ‘Dryads' seem to become active participants in the creative process. Were you interested in exploring the idea that music is not simply created by individuals, but also emerges from a dialogue with place, memory and nature?

Absolutely. This is one of the central ideas of the film. We live in a time dominated by noise, haste, the constant distractions of our screens and a certain dehumanization of our relationship with the world. Through Emil, Vasco and Joana, I wanted to explore a less anthropocentric perspective, one grounded in listening and in a humbler relationship with our surroundings.

Nature and chance contribute something essential to the creative process that lies beyond our control and even beyond our understanding. The landscape is not simply a backdrop or a source of inspiration; it becomes an active presence, almost another collaborator. It can suggest, interrupt, transform and redirect the music. I find something reassuring in accepting that creation is not entirely under our control. Perhaps learning to surrender part of that control is precisely what allows something new to happen. Chance and uncertainty are essential to my work, as they are for many filmmakers who embrace nonfiction.

articles.title: Imax Promotes Giovanni Dolci to COO Amid C-Suite Moves
articles.summary: He fills the newly created role, while Mark Welton is upped to president, strategic partnerships as the film technologies company sees momentum from a Hollywood box office resurgence.
articles.content:
Imax has promoted Giovanni Dolci to the newly created role of chief operating officer, overseeing the company's expanding global theater network.

Dolci, who joined Imax in 2012 and most recently served as chief commercial officer and executive vp, will relocate from London to New York City for his new role and report to Imax CEO Richard Gelfond. Building out its global theater footprint from beyond North America has long been a priority at the film technologies company as it rides momentum from having Chris Nolan's The Odyssey and other Hollywood tentpoles popping at the box office.

"Imax is a stronger, more global business than ever, and we continue to evolve and grow our leadership team to capture the many opportunities ahead. Gio has a deep understanding of our business, our partners, and our people at every level. He's been central to our growth for more than a decade, and his leadership will be critical in this next era of success for Imax," Gelfond said in a statement.

Imax also promoted Mark Welton from president, Imax global theatres, to the new role of president, strategic partnerships, and also reporting to Gelfond.

Welton will lead partnerships beyond the company's core theatrical business, working content programmers on new business opportunities across sports, events, and consumer brands. He has done earlier partnerships with the NHL, Major League Baseball and NBCUniversal, including the opening ceremony for the 2024 Paris Olympics.

“Mark has been instrumental in building Imax, and few people know our company and industry like he does. He is exactly the right person to turn the strength of our brand into new sources of growth," Gelfond added.

articles.title: Marvel Carefully Orchestrated the Return of Every Major Avengers Villain in 2026 Ahead of Doomsday
articles.summary: Following the conclusion of the Infinity Saga in 2019, MCU fans were left wondering how the franchise could top the universe-ending threat of Thanos. The answer, it turned out, was to both scale back and expand out at the same time. The Multiverse Saga widened the stakes to not just the MCU’s prime universe but […]
articles.content:
Even though the overall arc of the past few years hasn’t been as delicately crafted as the initial MCU era, the Multiverse Saga has introduced several fan favorites, such as Florence Pugh’s Yelena Belova , and cherished story arcs, like the recently concluded WandaVision trilogy. Of course, after Marvel conditioned audiences to expect everything to connect, Marvel has been scrambling a bit since dramatically shifting its plans for new Avengers films . And part of that has seemingly been to circle back around to every major foe the Avengers have gone up against, starting with one whose return was baked into the fabric of Avengers: Endgame .

At the time, news that Tom Hiddleston’s Loki would serve as the primary threat in The Avengers felt like a risky move. After all, Hiddleston was still a relatively unknown star, and if the film had fallen apart, the MCU would have faced a potentially fatal blow. Thankfully, Loki was a formidable enough foe to inspire the Avengers to assemble for the first time. And even better, the reveal that he was working on behalf of Thanos himself set into motion the overarching storyline that would persist throughout the rest of the Infinity Saga. The Loki Disney+ series then plumbed new depths of the character, offering him as an invaluable ally to the Avengers, as his surprise appearance in the final moments of Avengers Endgame: Encore confirms.

Even more recently, the MCU has revived James Spader’s Ultron on VisionQuest . Not seen in the live-action MCU since 2015’s Avengers: Age of Ultron , the character previously made an unforgettable appearance in the animated series What If…? in his Infinity Ultron form. But VisionQuest , while not quite redeeming him, presents a more complicated Ultron who seems just as fascinated with humanity as he is considering how to destroy them. Not to delve too deeply into spoiler territory, but VisionQuest ends in such a way that Ultron could still be in play as the MCU heads into Avengers: Doomsday . Will he have a role? Perhaps not, but the timing is intriguingly loaded with possibilities.

To date, Robert Downey Jr.’s Doctor Doom has only made the briefest of appearances throughout the MCU, all of them in the last couple of years. This is not only a symptom of Downey’s relatively recent return to the franchise but, more importantly, the MCU’s shift away from Kang as the Big Bad, at least heading into the fifth Avengers film . Marvel has been hard at work to establish Doom before his formal introduction, but it has also seemingly gone out of its way to reintroduce Josh Brolin’s Thanos to the forefront of fans’ minds, thanks to Avengers Endgame: Encore .

Certainly, the rerelease of Avengers: Endgame is mostly concerned with retconning the events of that film as a direct prequel to Avengers: Doomsday . But it also serves as a nice refresher course for fans who have strayed from their MCU devotion in the years since. As of now, Thanos remains the only major enemy of the Avengers to not receive some fresh screen time. But speculation still persists that Brolin could reprise his role soon, a move that would likely end with an ill-fated confrontation with Doom . If this happens, it would instantly give the MCU the ability to reaffirm the might of Doctor Doom, dismissing the lack of lead-up to the character.

Should Thanos return in Avengers: Doomsday ? Let us know in the comments below!

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters on December 18, 2026.

articles.title: Detective Comics #1115 Masterfully Adapts One of Batman's Most Underrated Stories for Superman (Review)
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics "Bruce Wayne: Murderer Turned Fugitive" is an underrated but classic Batman tale in which his civilian identity is accused of murdering his ex-girlfriend. In response, the Dark Knight chose to abandon his life as Bruce Wayne, and the fallout focused on his exploration of what that means and the Bat-Family's relentless pursuit of cracking the […]
articles.content:
Don't take this to mean that this is a simple rehash of the original, either. This is squarely a murder mystery centered around Superman , with Batman being the detective. It knows exactly how to make that concept work, and what emotion beats it needs to focus on with masterful characterization and control of what we're shown. This is a fantastic start to an arc that's guaranteed to keep us on the edge of our seats, from the fantastic opening to the cliffhanger ending.

This issue begins with the murder of the daughter of Smallville's mayor, Esme Brennan, with Clark Kent being the prime suspect. He immediately turns himself in, while Batman jumps onto the case. I'm always a sucker for depictions of Batman's detective process, and this issue more than delivers. We see him investigate where the body was dropped and the corpse itself, all while attempting to assure the rest of the Justice League and keep them from interfering in his investigation. Meanwhile, Clark is put in jail while everyone questions what they're doing, arresting Clark Kent. In the end, Batman finally visits Clark, where the Man of Tomorrow forces Batman to ask him if he did it. Clark's answer, concerningly, is that he doesn't know.

This is a thrilling plot that delivers on its premise expertly so far, but the real meat of the story is definitely in how it handles the fallout. Obviously, Clark didn't murder anyone, and everyone in the comic knows that too. Nobody treats him as if he did for an instant, and even the police officer who arrests him is apologetic and does everything to make Clark comfortable. Nobody believes he did this, but they're all following procedure to find the truth. A lesser version of this story would create artificial drama by having everyone question whether Superman was capable of this, which would only drag the story down, as it's Superman, so the answer is obvious.

While examining the scene, Batman even finds evidence that could point to Clark. Given that the body was dropped in the fields without tracks and she seemed to fall from above, it points to someone who can fly. He notices these things as a detective, but never lets that make his belief waver. The story smartly focuses on the inherent drama of Clark being framed, and even throws a curveball with the revelation that Clark doesn't know if he did this or not. That implies that either he doesn't remember that night, or that he was involving Esme in something that got her killed. Either way, that cliffhanger provides ten times more tension than anyone but Clark wondering if he did it, as this is something Clark would worry about because he doesn't see himself as unshakeable like everyone else does. This is perfect characterization for both leads, and I am beyond excited for the next issue.

Janín's art has been incredible for his entire run on Detective Comics (2016), but this might just be his best issue yet. His style has a picturesque, realistic approach that builds itself in the details. Everywhere the eye is drawn is layered with rich details and impact, with the edges being more vague, but carrying enough design cues that it's incredibly easy to fill in everything, which adds so much to the experience. My personal favorite page is definitely the one framed in Clark's POV. His outstretched arms over Smallville is a beautiful image, and the police station's inside and outside are the perfect example of the expert use of details.

However, the real heavy-hitter in this issue is definitely the lighting. Every shot is beautiful on its own, but they are all elevated to the next level by lights that add a whole new dimension. The best examples of this all come from the police station. Clark's talk with Larry has a wonderful electric shine that helps emphasize the strangeness of the location. Clark and Batman's talk is beautifully rendered, using shadows to contrast and highlight both men while adding so much more impact to the scene. Even the gentle red glow of Clark's eyes as he uses his X-Ray vision is a little touch that does volumes. Batman and Superman are both magnificent in this scene, and I definitely want to see more like it.

What do you think really went down with Esme's murder, and how do you think Clark ties into it? Let us know your theory in the comments below!

EXCLUSIVE: We recently announced the first Friday the 13th film in nearly two decades — and now, we have new details on the project, which wraps production today.

The film, directed by the previously announced Steve Miner, is titled Jason . It's slated for a worldwide theatrical release on Friday, Aug. 13, 2027, with Cineverse overseeing its North American distribution.

The ensemble cast is led by Schuyler White ( Haunt ) as Jason Voorhees, the enigmatic masked murderer at the heart of the slasher series, and Natalie Alyn Lind ( Dutton Ranch ) as “final girl” Lauren.

When you put all that together you get something special. This franchise has had many strong female leads, but her performance might just be the strongest this franchise has ever had.”

Jason marks the 13th entry of Friday the 13th , an iconic horror franchise that launched with a namesake 1980 slasher. Working from a script by emerging screenwriter David Fliegel, Miner returned to the director's chair after introducing Jason's machete in Friday the 13th Part II and unveiling his hockey mask for the first time in Friday the 13th Part III . The film was made independently to afford the Barsamian family, which financed and produced and control the franchise through their company Horror, Inc., total creative control.

Cunningham, the original Friday the 13th watches as a group of counselors at Camp Crystal Lake, preparing to reopen the summer camp, are stalked and killed by an unseen assailant, while the memory of a boy who drowned there years earlier hangs over the grounds. Produced independently for roughly $550,000 and acquired by Paramount in a bidding war, the film provided the foundation for a durable, low-budget sequel machine, with Paramount releasing early entries and and Warner Bros./New Line joining as distributor from the '90s on. The original film surprised with the revelation of ( SPOILER ) matriarch Pamela Voorhees as the murderous antagonist, while later entries embraced the machete-wielding Jason himself as the franchise's terrifying driving force.

Over the decades, Friday the 13th has spawned video games, immersive experiences, comic books, collectibles, apparel and more, alongside the films. Horror, Inc. launched the Jason Universe to usher in a new era of expansion in the franchise in 2024, and most recently, the franchise has been back in circulation via Crystal Lake , Peacock and A24's prequel series, which premiered all eight episodes on Oct. 15.

articles.title: New York Knicks Star Josh Hart Inks Two-Book Deal With HarperCollins (Exclusive)
articles.summary: The NBA star will publish a memoir next year, and a children's book after that.
articles.content:
New York Knicks guard Josh Hart has inked a two-book deal with News Corp.'s HarperCollins, The Hollywood Reporter has learned.

Hart will write a memoir, Live to Serve , which will be released in July of next year, and a children's book, which will be released at a later date. The memoir will include Hart's humor, faith, and heart, and will chronicle his college career at Villanova through this year's NBA championship.

Senior VP & publisher Lisa Sharkey and senior VP & publisher Nancy Inteli negotiated U.S. and Commonwealth rights to the books with Anthony Mattero at CAA.

"I'm honored to be able to show readers how faith can shape the way they work, lead, compete, parent, and live their lives," says Hart. "I'm writing for athletes and fans, but also for parents, coaches, young people, business leaders, and anyone who has felt overlooked or wondered whether the work happening outside the spotlight still matters. My faith journey means everything to me as a player, a parent, a husband, and a human and I'm excited to bring readers along with me so they too can Live to Serve.

“Josh Hart is the heartbeat of the New York Knicks. Whether he moves with the ball or without it, he serves his teammates and the greater good, and he gives glory to God first and foremost,” says Sharkey. “This book will inspire fans to learn more about Josh and will entertain them with his sense of humor, but most importantly, it will remind readers that on the court, a higher power always wins the game of life."

"Josh brings the same incredible energy to storytelling that he brings to the court," adds Inteli. "Like Josh himself, the picture book is full of warmth, humor, and especially heart. Families will want to read it again and again."

Launching Nov. 20, the capsule marks the latest release from GapStudio, the retailer's elevated fashion line overseen by Posen, Gap Inc.'s executive vice president and creative director. The new collection takes a more dressed-up approach to the brand's signature American sportswear. Centered on a black palette, with accents of royal blue, deep red, winter white and neutral tones, you'll find in the capsule denim, poplin and knitwear — this time with with sharper tailoring and exaggerated proportions. Standout pieces include a contoured rib maxi dress ($268), a structured denim jacket ($168), a denim double-breasted blazer ($198) and high-rise seamed stirrup jeans ($148).

One of the collection's more playful designs is the Brannan Bear Sherpa Jacket ($268), a faux-fur outerwear piece complete with bear ears inspired by Gap's longtime mascot.

“For Winter 2026, we wanted to move beyond traditional occasion wear with versatile pieces designed to be worn from day to night,” Posen said in a statement. “There's still that level of drama with thoughtful tailoring and exaggerated lines, but it's balanced by a focused palette that feels elegant and wearable.”

EJAE rose to international prominence as the singing voice of Rumi, the lead character in Netflix's “KPop Demon Hunters,” and co-writer of the film's breakout hit “Golden.” The song became a global chart phenomenon and earned the singer-songwriter a Golden Globe for best original song. Her appearance in the GapStudio campaign represents another crossover into fashion for the musician, who previously worked behind the scenes writing songs for K-pop acts including Red Velvet, aespa and Twice.

The release continues Posen's efforts to elevate Gap's fashion credentials through GapStudio, which launched as a more design-focused extension of the retailer's everyday wardrobe. Earlier this fall, the brand unveiled a 20-piece collection modeled by Esther McGregor and Alton Mason.

The GapStudio Winter 2026 collection will be available beginning Nov. 20 on Gap.com and at select Gap stores, with prices ranging from $54 to $268.

It's a film brought by a promising team, a delicate emerging voice. Therefore, the jury decided to award a film that takes us to Kyrgyzstan, Stitch by Stitch directed by Alina Baitokova, produced by Adilet Karzhoev and Marianna Kaat."

The award for Best Pitch Project comes with a €1,500 prize.

The award for Best Roundtable Project is accompanied by a €1,500 prize.

In other IDFA Forum prizes, the award for Best Rough Cut Project went to Resisting Residents by Nikos Pilos and Arsinoi Pilou.

" Resisting Residents is a powerful reminder of how cinema can champion what we believe in," wrote said jurors Chalida Uabumrungjit and Cleo Veger. "This brave documentary captures a community standing firm for their homes, their dignity, and their right to live together, proving that film can be an essential voice for justice and human solidarity. We were moved by the courage of the residents, who take in newcomers, face their own conflicts and fight eviction together, and by a film team honest enough to show all of it. Shot by a two-person crew living inside the community, it's close, trusting and alive, and we can't wait to see it finished."

The award comes with a €1,500 prize.

Resisting Residents also won the InVision Subtitling Award, presented by Walter Groenewegen, which provides closed captioning and subtitles for a project presented in the Rough Cut category.

The IDFA DocLab Forum Award for Best Project was claimed by This Pleasant Lady by Victoria Mapplebeck. "The jury unanimously agrees that this project is inspirational and addresses serious subjects in an irreverent but impactful way that will engage with audiences no matter of their cultural background or ages. The spirit of the project and the artist fits the vibe of IDFA DocLab. We're also now encouraged to create our own fuck you list!" said jury members Min-Wei Kuo and David Massey.

The award is accompanied by a €1,500 prize.

Jurors additionally recognized Time Hunter XR: Colonial Protocols by Mark Mushiva and Daniel Chein. "The jury want to give a Special Mention to a project that really thinks carefully about how the experience will take audiences on a journey that explores themes of time travel, sci-fi, and embodied archive. The project creates an imaginative and engaging experience that brings forward the perspectives of people whose voices deserve to be heard, and histories that deserve to be told."

Latido Films , a sales agent on Rodrigo Sorogoyen's "The Beasts," Netflix mega-hit "The Platform" and Ventana Sur 2025 breakout "The Whisper," is bringing to market " S.O.S ," a blue sky Caribbean island rom-com which renews Latido's relationship with top Colombian producer Diego F. Ramírez at 64A Films .

"S.O.S." also has a first teaser trailer, shared in exclusivity with Variety . Related Stories Weta FX and TAICCA Partner to Turn Taiwan Into an AI Screen Production Hub for Asia Hollywood Has Flipped on GenAI, Says 'Avatar' VFX House Weta FX Chief: 'If You Don’t Have an AI Strategy, Don’t Bother'

A producer on Sundance hit "Dog Eat Dog," a founding stone in Colombia's modern film industry, Ramírez has gone on to produce one of Colombia's most ambitious non-streamer shows, “Escobar, el Patron del Mal," as well as Toronto premiere "The Dog Washer" and "Killing Jesus," the feature film debut of Laura Mora, director of "One Hundred Years of Solitude." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

In a lighter turn for tougher times, 'S.O.S' weighs in in two ways as a crowdpleaser, a blue sky – literally – comedy, set on an uninhabited Caribbean islet, which also offers the lures of romance and second-chance drama.

In it, Jaime, a once hot-shot photographer, is shipwrecked on the white-sand beach island with Cata and Valeria, the stars of an upcoming telenovela, rated as his country's most beautiful women.

Paradise? The sojourn sets off as hell. Cata, a post peak-fame actress has been reduced to playing the mother of Valeria, an influencer who broke out aping Cata. The two hate each other's guts. Battling to survive, however, all three have to smooth their differences and work together in what morphs into a survival adventure and second chance story where they re-connect with the far more sincere people they once were. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Manuela González (Netflix's ‘Fake Profile') plays Cata, Juan Fernando Sánchez ("La Huésped") Jaime and María Camilo Giraldo ("The Ritual") Valeria.

Fast-paced, but allowing a glimpse of key plot beats, the teaser begins with the shipwreck, flashes back to the photo shoot – "my aunts were your fans," Valeria tells Cata cattily during makeup – then an establishing shot of the isle in the middle of a vast nowhere.

The trio have food at hand, such as a coconut, but they don't know how to open them. time exiled from a community hammock. They build a hammock, but Jaime is banished. They seek refuge in a cave, which is infested by bats.

There is, however, a hint in the teaser's parting shot, however, that love could be in the air between Cata and Jaime.

"S.O.S." is produced by Colombia's 64 Films, headed by Ramírez and Nancy Fernández for 64A Films, with Hans García and Ingrid Cruz for the Dominican Republic's Hannah Films.

"The tone that I'm thinking of is ‘The Blue Lagoon," with the paradisiacal exuberance of ‘Ticket to Paradise,'" said director Nicolas Reyes ("Decisions: Some Win and Others Lose"), also a first AD on the Colombian unit of "Paddington in. Peru."

"For a sales agent, the most interesting and stimulating to be in on a project from its birth, as was the case with 'S.O.S.' said Latido Films Head of International Sales Juan Torres. "The understanding with 64A is remarkable and we are confident this will have a knock-on in the film's commercial results."

EXCLUSIVE : Imax has promoted a pair of executives to newly created roles as it expands its leadership.

Giovanni (Gio) Dolci was named the big screen exhibitor's first chief operating officer, reporting to CEO Rich Gelfond. The executive, currently based in London as EVP and chief commercial officer, will transfer to New York with expanded oversight of Global Theatres and Technology in addition to his current leadership of the Global Sales, and Streaming and Consumer Technology teams.

He'll serve as a key day-to-day strategic partner for Gelfond. Related Stories News Imax CEO Wades Into 'Cliff Booth' Debate: "Frankly, I Don't Understand" News 'The Odyssey' Powers Record Q3 For Imax, Stock Jumps, CEO On Platform's "Power And Potential"

articles.title: 5 Young Avengers/Champions Members Marvel Needs to Introduce Before the Team's MCU Debut
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics The Marvel Cinematic Universe has been building up its roster for the next generation of heroes, whether it is the Young Avengers or the Champions. Kamala Khan debuted on Disney+ before making her way into the big-screen movie The Marvels. Kate Bishop debuted on the Hawkeye Disney+ series, and America Chavez debuted in the movie […]
articles.content:
Right now, it seems like the new project won't be the Young Avengers , but will instead be The Champions, and it will be a movie instead of a Disney+ streaming series. No matter what they call it, it's likely to be a mix of the two comic teams, with names like Wiccan and Kate Bishop coming from the Young Avengers while Kamala Khan and Ironheart were on the Champions. With that said, there are some heroes who still need to arrive.

Don't expect Viv Vision to appear in the MCU anytime soon, at least not based on what happened in VisionQuest . There was no room on the Vision Disney+ show for creating a robot family because it was all about him finding his original family. That said, there are a lot of reasons to bring Viv Vision into the MCU because she is a great character. It could be done in another way, especially considering how Jocasta had her origin changed in the series. Avengers: Secret Wars could even offer that opportunity.

Viv debuted in Vision #1 (2015) by Tom King and Gabriel Hernández Walta. The Vision built her as a teenage daughter alongside a wife, Virginia, and a twin brother, Vin . He combined his own brainwaves with Virginia's to create the twins. She joined the Champions in Champions #1, and much of her history had her struggling to understand humanity, including a moment in the “Outlawed” storyline where she betrayed her friends because she believed they were being irrational.

Marvel Boy is a Kree named Noh-Varr, and he debuted in Marvel Boy #1 (2000) by Grant Morrison and J.G. Jones. He was a member of the Young Avengers. Young Avengers #1 (2013) saw him on a team with Wiccan, Hulkling, Hawkeye, Loki, and Miss America, and he eventually entered into a relationship with Kate Bishop. He also has a long history in Marvel before the Young Avengers, as he was part of Norman Osborn's Dark Avengers, pretending to be Captain Mar-Vell.

While Noh-Varr hasn't debuted in the MCU yet, there is a place where he could show up, specifically through Carol Danvers' connections to the Kree, and this could connect him with Kamala Khan. Hailee Steinfeld's Kate Bishop is already in the MCU, and The Marvels ends with Kamala recruiting her for a new team, which could lead her to find the young Kree, especially with the entire alien race in chaos.

Brawn is someone who really needs to be in the MCU, and why he hasn't debuted yet remains a mystery. He is Amadeus Cho, and as Cho, he has been a partner of both Hulk and Hercules in the comics, but he has only been teased in the MCU. His mother, Dr. Helen Cho (Claudia Kim), appeared in the 2015 film Avengers: Age of Ultron when she was forced to work on building a new body for Ultron. However, Amadeus has still not appeared himself.

Cho became a Hulk after he saved the day when the original Hulk's body began to overload. How Marvel could introduce Cho remains to be seen, although it could be another addition to Avengers: Secret Wars if there is a realm of Hulks on Battleworld. However, whatever happens, the current group of teenage heroes doesn't have a powerhouse yet, and unless Marvel plans to use Skaar, Amadeus Cho is the next best bet.

There are strong rumors that Sam Alexander is coming to the MCU. Marvel is working on a Nova movie with Richard Rider, and that would be the best place to debut Sam Alexander. Sam debuted in Marvel Point One #1 (2011) by Jeph Loeb and Ed McGuinness. His costume is the same as Rider's Nova, and he wears a Nova helmet that once belonged to his own father. While he wasn't part of the Nova Corps thanks to his age and lack of training, he joined the Champions on Earth instead.

This actually compares well to Richard Rider, who was part of the New Warriors as a teenager. With Nova being one of the youngest members of the Champions, it makes a lot of sense for him to be part of the team in the MCU. The original team had the close friendship of Kamala Khan, Miles Morales, and Nova at its forefront, and while the MCU might change that to Kamala, Ironheart, and Kate Bishop, Nova deserves his spot.

The one teenage hero who has to appear, and one who is really non-negotiable, is Hulkling. This is because Hulkling is Wiccan's partner and one of the first members of the Young Avengers . Having Hulkling and Wiccan's relationship is something that has to be a big part of this new team of teenage heroes. Teddy Altman debuted with Wiccan in Young Avengers #1 (2005) by Allan Heinberg and Jim Cheung, and they have been connected ever since.

He is the son of the Kree hero Mar-Vell and the Skrull princess Anelle, which made him heir to two empires that have been at war for ages. This led him to become the emperor of the Kree-Skrull Empire for a period before that ended in the recent “Imperial” cosmic event. In whatever way Marvel has him show up, Hulkling has to be there for the new Champions or Young Avengers movie, and he needs to finally connect with Wiccan to make this team complete.

Who do you want to see on the Young Avengers or Champions team in the MCU? Let us know what you want to see in the comments below.

Currently, the Mothership, NCIS: New York , and NCIS : Origins are airing, and come early 2027, NCIS : Sydney will be joining the lineup. Even though it’s exciting that we’re finally going back down under, some fans can’t help but bring up the other shows from the franchise that were unfortunately canceled.

Just this week, he official NCIS Instagram confirmed Sydney Season 4's premiere for this coming January. After that, plenty of people took to the comments to share their thoughts. And not all of the sentiments were positive. Some fans are currently pointing out the sacrifices that have been made to make room for Sydney . That includes cutting Origins ’ third season in half , while both NCIS and newbie New York get full seasons. Others are still hurt over NCIS: Los Angeles and NCIS: Hawai’i 's cancellations, as well as the (still-fresh) cancellation of Tony & Ziva :

As someone who is a fan of every single NCIS show, I’m definitely still hurt over having to say goodbye to these axed shows far too soon. Hawai’i ’s cancellation definitely blindsided me and others, including series star Vanessa Lachey. Quite frankly, I’m still wondering exactly why the Eye Network decided to end it.

As for Tony & Ziva , fans were hoping CBS would pick up the series after Paramount+ canceled it, but unfortunately, that was not in the cards. It's great that co-lead Michael Weatherly is back on NCIS , but it’s still just not the same. Even amid the announcement of the New York spinoff, there were plenty of detractors speaking out about the canceled NCIS shows . While I understand that the network TV is a business, I can still empathize with the sentiments.

Meanwhile, Sydney ’s return marks a change for the franchise that is upsetting fans. Some viewers have been sharing their displeasure over the fact that both Sydney and Origins are not getting full seasons. Instead, the two shows are getting only 10 episodes for their respective seasons. It’s understandable that CBS would do this, given that there’s already too many shows on the schedule, but a 10-installment run just feels way too short.

That being said, I will gladly take what I can get, as a 10-episode order is better than nothing. On that note, I'd imagine that plenty of franchise devotees will continue to tune in for the shows that are still airing. However, I don't expect many of them to stop carrying torches for the canceled shows anytime soon.

At the very least, NCIS: Sydney will finally be returning for Season 4 on Tuesday, January 26 on CBS, streaming the next day with a Paramount+ subscription .
